text:
elaine-support: Ken from Acme reported a spike of 429s on their Dedicated pool (ded-nyc-3) starting ~09:02 UTC. They saw sustained errors for ~3m, app-facing latency jumped. customer says they didn't change traffic patterns. attaching initial repro and logs below.

mike-oncall: pulling logs now. any tenant id?

elaine-support: tenant: acme-enterprise-78, API key masked. sample curl they ran: 
```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"hello"}'
```
They reported ~120 r/s sustained, bursts to 300 r/s for ~20s.

raj-eng-runtime: quick theory: dedicated pool has per-tenant soft rate cap recently changed in config release, might be applying per-second rather than per-minute. grabbing quota config for ded-nyc-3.

deploy-bot: release 2026.02.11-rc3 applied to cluster ded-nyc-3 at 2026-02-11T08:50:12Z

raj-eng-runtime: config snippet from control plane (sanitized): 
```
tenant_rate_limits: 
  default: 100rps
  acme-enterprise-78: 100rpm  # intended minutes but flag parsed as rps due to parser bug
```

raj-eng-runtime: confirm: parser bug discussed in PR #443 accidentally treats values with trailing `m` as `ms`? looks like our migration mapped `rpm` to `rps` for dedicated pools.

mike-oncall: can we repro locally by sending 150 r/s to a tenant on a dev ded pool? I'll spin load generator.

sophia-cs: Ken says their billing shows only ~3% higher tokens; traffic should not have been flagged. they rely on steady throughput. ticket #CS-4599 opened.

autoscale-bot: autoscaler observed CPU pressure and scaled to +1 replica at 09:04:21 UTC, but scale-up lagged ~45s due to node allocation. peak queue depth recorded: 430.

mike-oncall: repro done on ded-dev-1: sending 200 r/s triggered 429s within 30s. stacktrace shows throttle hit at rate_limiter.go:142 with key tenant:acme-enterprise-78. attaching minimal repro command: 
```
for i in `seq 1 300`; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\n\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"$URL/v1/generate\" & done
```

raj-eng-runtime: root cause: misinterpreted quota unit combined with conservative default for dedicated pools. result: acme was limited to 100 rps not 100 rpm as intended. behavior: sustained bursts -> immediate 429s, autoscaler couldn't catch up fast enough -> queued requests and latency spike.

elaine-support: customer impact note: short outages 09:02-09:06 UTC, ~2.4k failed requests, they reported downstream error pages. They want quota corrected and request retroactive credits for failed calls.

raj-eng-runtime: remediation steps: 1) hotfix parser to respect `rpm` as per-minute units and roll to control plane. 2) temporarily bump acme-enterprise-78 tenant cap to 1000rps on ded-nyc-3 while we roll hotfix. 3) add canary check to alert if per-tenant cap < 10% of observed sustained rate.

mike-oncall: I've applied temporary override: `tenant_rate_limits.acme-enterprise-78=1000rps` on ded-nyc-3 via admin CLI. monitoring now shows 200 r/s with <1% 429s.

deploy-bot: admin change recorded by ui-admin at 2026-02-11T09:10:05Z

raj-eng-runtime: will open PR for parser fix, add unit tests for `rpm`/`rps`/`rph` parsing. tagging infra and ml-runtime.

sophia-cs: I updated the CS ticket and notified Ken. he asked for a short postmortem and credits.

ken-acme: thanks team. impact was visible in our dashboards. appreciate the temporary lift and a timeline for fix + credits.

raj-eng-runtime: ETA for parser patch + canary: 6 hours for patch + rollout to control plane, then 24h monitoring window. will follow up with changelog.

elaine-support: next actions for support: confirm fix when rolled, coordinate credits with finance, and follow up with customer after 24h stability window. marking as high-priority and assigning to raj and mike. :thumbsup:

mike-oncall: adding a short-term alert: if queue depth > 200 and 429% > 1% for any tenant on dedicated pools, page oncall.

raj-eng-runtime: noted. will update runbook entry to warn about this parsing edge case.

sophia-cs: Ken — I'll DM you the incident timeline and the ticket link.

ken-acme: got it, thanks everyone.
